items.name: hidden attribute (Hidden / Hidden Until Found, beforematch, ancestor revealing)
items.what: Enumerated hidden with until-found state: content-visibility:hidden instead of display:none, find-in-page and fragment navigation reveal it, firing bubbling beforematch and removing hidden; ancestor revealing algorithm also opens closed details. Elements stay active (forms submit, scripts run). Spec forbids hidden for tab panels.
items.gain: Inference: a module could reveal searchable collapsed regions (until-found) and listen for beforematch to sync state, plus guard against author CSS that overrides display/content-visibility (spec warns at interactions.md:93,97).
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap collapse/accordion hides with .collapse display:none (not until-found); tab panes hide panels the spec says hidden must not hide

items.name: Page visibility (visibilityState, visibilitychange, VisibilityStateEntry)
items.what: Document visibility state hidden/visible, document.hidden, a bubbling visibilitychange event, and performance entries of type visibility-state with timestamps.
items.gain: Inference: a module could pause or resume work (timers, media, polling) on visibility and record visibility timing; no UI component.
items.overlap: none (Bootstrap carousel pauses on visibility internally, but no exposed component)

items.name: Inert subtrees and the inert attribute (modal dialog blocking)
items.what: Inert nodes: no hit-testing, no selection, non-editable, ignored by find-in-page, not focusable, hidden from accessibility APIs. Modal dialog in top layer makes the rest of the document inert. inert attribute marks a subtree; spec says there is no default visual style and authors should mark inert regions visibly; use disabled for single form controls instead.
items.gain: Inference: a module could mark loading regions inert with a visible overlay (spec example at :291-335), e.g. over a form or table while it loads.
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap modal/offcanvas use their own focus trap and backdrop instead of inert; a loading-overlay pattern has no counterpart (spinners are styles only)
items.fit: Spec example is a form plus a table marked inert while loading (interactions.md:294-332); the orkestrel form and table packages are not described in these sources

items.name: User activation (sticky, transient, history-action; navigator.userActivation)
items.what: Per-Window activation timestamps; sticky vs transient vs history-action activation; activation-triggering events (keydown except Esc, mousedown, pointerdown mouse, pointerup non-mouse, touchend); API gating levels (sticky-gated, transient-gated, transient-consuming, history-action-consuming); navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive / isActive.
items.gain: Inference: a module could check isActive before calling gated APIs (clipboard, fullscreen, popups, CloseWatcher beyond free slot) and fall back gracefully.

items.name: Activation behavior, ToggleEvent, CommandEvent (command / commandfor, popovertarget)
items.what: Elements' activation behavior (button, a[href], details, popovertarget). button command/commandfor dispatch CommandEvent (command string, source element) to the controlled element, e.g. show-modal, toggle-popover. ToggleEvent (toggle, beforetoggle) with oldState/newState on details, dialog, popovers. Rules: commandfor should pair with command; popovertarget must reference a popover.
items.gain: Inference: a module could handle custom commands declaratively via commandfor and observe toggle/beforetoggle, with no JS-wired triggers.
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap data-bs-toggle/data-bs-target triggers for modal, collapse, dropdown, offcanvas cover the same declarative-trigger role

items.name: Focus (focusable areas, tabindex, sequential navigation, focus APIs, autofocus)
items.what: Focusable area definition (rendered, not inert, not disabled; inherently focusable or tabindex). tabindex rules: valid integer; -1 is focusable but not Tab-reachable; 0 is in DOM order; positive is an authoring smell; dialog must not have tabindex; tabindex in inert is unreachable. :focus, :focus-within, :focus-visible. focus(options), blur(), activeElement, hasFocus(). autofocus: at most one per document; useless inside inert.
items.gain: Inference: a module could provide roving tabindex, focus restore, and dev-time checks for these rules (positive tabindex, duplicate autofocus, autofocus inside inert).
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap modal/offcanvas focustrap and dropdown keyboard navigation are internal, not a standalone focus module

items.name: Keyboard shortcuts (accesskey)
items.what: accesskey is an ordered set of unique space-separated single code point tokens; duplicates or multi-character tokens are errors; two elements should not share a key; UA picks the assigned key and may expose it.
items.gain: Inference: a module could check accesskey conflicts and show assigned keys.

items.name: Editing (contenteditable, designMode, execCommand, spellcheck, writingsuggestions, autocapitalize, autocorrect, inputmode, enterkeyhint, draggable)
items.what: contenteditable true/false/plaintext-only (missing = inherit); editing hosts are focusable; inert overrides editability. document.designMode; legacy execCommand; enumerated hints spellcheck, writingsuggestions, autocapitalize, autocorrect, inputmode (none,text,tel,url,email,numeric,decimal,search), enterkeyhint (enter,done,go,next,previous,search,send). draggable is true/false.
items.gain: Inference: a module could provide inline editing on plaintext-only hosts (e.g. editable table cells) and correct input hints on form controls; best-practice section 6.8.3 is non-normative with no checkable rule.
items.overlap: none (Bootstrap has no editor; form controls are styles only)
items.fit: Inference: inputmode/enterkeyhint/autocapitalize hints fit a form package; contenteditable cells could fit a table package. The packages are not described in these sources

items.name: Find-in-page (details and hidden=until-found)
items.what: A match inside closed details opens it; a match inside hidden=until-found fires beforematch and removes hidden; a match updates selection and scrolls into view. ::details-content must not be display:none and until-found must compute to content-visibility:hidden.
items.gain: Inference: collapsed or paginated content stays findable if a module uses details or until-found and handles beforematch instead of display:none.
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap collapse/accordion hide content with display:none, which find-in-page cannot reach

items.name: Close requests and CloseWatcher
items.what: Close request is the platform dismiss signal (Esc on desktop, Back on Android) closing the topmost popover, modal dialog, or CloseWatcher. One free watcher without transient activation; modal dialogs and popovers register implicitly. new CloseWatcher() with requestClose(), close(), destroy(), cancel/close events.
items.gain: Inference: a module could give non-dialog surfaces (a sidebar, an in-place editor) the same Esc/Back dismissal stack.
items.overlap: Partial: Bootstrap modal, offcanvas, dropdown handle Esc with their own keydown listeners (no Android Back)

items.name: Implicit ARIA roles (scoped appendix)
items.what: Table of implicit roles per element: forms (select combobox vs listbox, output status, progress progressbar, meter, input types, input+list combobox), tables (table, rowgroup, row, cell or gridcell in grid, columnheader/rowheader by scope), interactive (details group, dialog). States it is not an ARIA validity auditor.
items.gain: Inference: modules on native elements keep implicit roles rather than adding ARIA; a table module must not override display off the table model without compensating roles.
items.fit: Table roles (aria.md:106-116, 169-172) and form roles (aria.md:118-144) are the native semantics a table or form package would rely on

items.name: Content categories (interactive content and others)
items.what: Interactive content members: a[href], audio[controls], button, details, embed, iframe, img[usemap], input not hidden, label, object[usemap], select, textarea, video[controls]. Transparent model, flow/phrasing/palpable/script-supporting categories; script and template allowed inside table and list models.
items.gain: Inference: a module that injects controls must respect no-interactive-descendant rules (no button inside a or button).

items.name: form
items.what: The UA provides HTMLFormElement with elements, requestSubmit(submitter), reset(), checkValidity() (fires invalid at each failing control), reportValidity() (native UI for the first failure only), novalidate, and method=dialog. invalid events fire before submit.
items.gain: The UA bubble shows one message at a time. The guide says invalid events let an author 'display a full error summary rather than relying on the browser's single-message default'. Authors repeat FormData snapshots, dirty and touched tracking, and an error summary. A module could read form.elements and FormData without restyling. Inference: validation feedback overlaps Bootstrap; an unsaved-changes guard does not.
items.overlap: Validation feedback is excluded (.was-validated, .is-valid and .is-invalid; catalog:96). The unsaved-changes guard (guards/) passes (catalog:167).
items.fit: orkestrel form package (inferred; package not read). The elements guide's own createForm notes map requestSubmit, checkValidity, the formdata event, willValidate, and touched tracking (forms.md:1024-1060).

items.name: label
items.what: The UA provides for= and implicit wrapping, activation forwarding to the labeled control, label.control, and the live control.labels NodeList, which is null on type=hidden.
items.gain: Nothing behavioral to add. Inference: a module can read labels for announcements, such as error text naming the field.

items.name: input (text, search, tel, url, email, password)
items.what: The UA provides typed text controls with autocomplete tokens (section-*, shipping and billing), inputmode keyboards, pattern, minlength and maxlength, and field-sizing. A select event fires on selection change. Rendered as inline-block one-line scroll containers 20 characters wide by default.
items.gain: Authors repeat password reveal, character counters for maxlength, and one-time-code handling. Inference: a counter writes to output, not a Bootstrap component.
items.overlap: Styled by .form-control; no JS. Search cancel button styling is excluded (catalog:118).

items.name: input (date, month, week, time, datetime-local, number)
items.what: The UA provides locale-presented pickers with an ISO 8601 wire format, and number with step, min, and max. Each is an inline-block about one line high.
items.gain: Scripts always see the wire format. Authors repeat locale display of submitted values, which pairs with time. A module driving these controls or showPicker() is excluded.
items.overlap: Excluded: native inputs Bootstrap styles, including the date and time types, number spin buttons, and showPicker() (catalog:118).

items.name: input type=range and type=color
items.what: Range is a non-devolvable slider; list= datalist values render as snap tick marks. Color is a color well with a picker, and list values appear in the picker.
items.gain: Authors repeat a live value readout, usually an output beside the range.

items.name: input type=checkbox and type=radio
items.what: The UA provides non-devolvable controls with no label, RadioNodeList through form[name], and command facets.
items.gain: Inference: a tri-state 'select all' checkbox (indeterminate) over a table is repeated author code. The guides did not state this.
items.overlap: .form-check, .btn-check toggles, and .form-switch; the switch attribute is excluded (catalog:122).

items.name: input type=file
items.what: The UA renders file names plus a ::file-selector-button. accept and multiple are supported.
items.gain: A drop zone is borderline-excluded.
items.overlap: .form-control with ::file-selector-button. The file drop zone is excluded as borderline (catalog:117).

items.name: button
items.what: The UA provides type submit, reset, or button, formaction and the other form* overrides, popovertarget, commandfor with command (built-in show-modal, close, request-close, show-popover, and custom -- commands that dispatch CommandEvent), and button layout.
items.gain: Custom -- commands let a module react declaratively to a trigger without data-bs wiring. Only --copy, --fullscreen, and --wake survive as trigger syntax.
items.overlap: .btn styles it. The Button toggle uses JS. Invoker commands as a router are excluded (catalog:101).

items.name: select, optgroup, option
items.what: The UA provides drop-down or list box (multiple, size), hr separators, customizable select (button with selectedcontent, rich option content, optgroup legend), and field-sizing. A drop-down supports base appearance.
items.gain: Customizable select is excluded.

items.name: datalist
items.what: Not rendered itself. It supplies option suggestions to input list= and has a phrasing-fallback mode.
items.gain: Excluded.

items.name: textarea
items.what: The UA provides a multiline plain-text control (text content model) with maxlength, wrap, and dirname. white-space is pre-wrap.
items.gain: field-sizing:content gives auto-grow natively. Authors repeat a remaining-character counter.

items.name: output
items.what: A listed, labelable, resettable result of a calculation. for= lists contributing IDs. It holds phrasing content.
items.gain: Authors hand-write oninput calculations, as in the guide's form oninput example. The catalog addendum already routes Copier confirmation text into the page's output.
items.overlap: none (no Bootstrap component found in these sources)

items.name: progress
items.what: Determinate (value/max) or indeterminate. Devolvable widget, 10em by 1em, with platform presentation.
items.gain: Excluded.

items.name: meter
items.what: A gauge with low, high, and optimum zones, 5em by 1em, devolvable.
items.gain: Borderline-excluded unless gauge zones are ruled a different concept.

items.name: fieldset and legend
items.what: fieldset[disabled] disables descendants (except the first legend) and excludes them from validation through willValidate. fieldset.elements is available. The UA renders the legend over the border; the anonymous content box inherits grid and flex.
items.gain: Inference: section-level validity or 'step' state per fieldset is repeated author code.
items.overlap: Bootstrap reboot styles them. The disabled fieldset counts toward the excluded busy-region concept (catalog:116).

items.name: details and summary
items.what: A disclosure with an open attribute and name exclusive groups. A coalesced toggle event fires. The UA shadow tree has a ::details-content slot with content-visibility:hidden when closed.
items.gain: Excluded: every addition is Collapse's. The spec forbids using details for tabs or menus.

items.name: dialog
items.what: The UA provides show(), showModal(), close(rv), requestClose(rv) (cancelable cancel event), returnValue, closedby (any, closerequest, none), light dismiss, beforetoggle and toggle ToggleEvent with source, focus restoration, the top layer, and ::backdrop.
items.gain: Excluded by ruling.

items.name: search
items.what: A landmark grouping search or filter controls. It holds flow content. The guide shows JS-only filtering with an output for 'no results'.
items.gain: Inference: a client-side filter over a list or table, announcing the result count through output, is repeated author code. No overlap appears in the catalog's Excluded rows.

items.name: menu
items.what: A semantic toolbar list of li commands. The guide says styling 'is up to the application'.
items.gain: Arrow-key toolbar navigation is the excluded focusgroup concept.
items.overlap: focusgroup and keyboard navigation are excluded (catalog:121); button groups.

items.name: time
items.what: Represents dates, times, offsets, or durations, with a machine-readable datetime attribute.
items.gain: Authors repeat locale and relative formatting.
items.overlap: none; relative time with Intl is shortlisted at rank 9 (catalog:137).

items.name: data
items.what: Pairs human content with a required machine value. The spec example uses it so a table sorting library can sort textual numbers.
items.gain: A sort key for the shortlisted table sorter.

items.name: table, caption, colgroup, col, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th, td
items.what: The DOM provides createTHead, insertRow, and deleteRow; rows ordered thead, then bodies, then tfoot; tr.rowIndex and sectionRowIndex; insertCell; cellIndex; th scope and abbr; headers; and the header-assignment algorithm. The UA renders separate borders, 2px spacing, bold th, a centered caption, and hidden rows with visibility:collapse.

items.overlap: .table styles it; no JS. Sorters pass (catalog:165).

items.name: img and picture/source
items.what: The UA provides srcset and sizes (including sizes=auto), loading=lazy, decoding, fetchpriority, decode() as a promise, and a controls attribute (fullscreen controls are implementation-defined). Rendering covers broken and alt states.
items.gain: width and height prevent layout shift on lazy images. decode() before insertion avoids dropped frames.

items.name: video, audio, track
items.what: The UA provides controls, poster, preload, playsinline, and track kinds (subtitles, captions, descriptions, chapters). Controls overlay without layout change. video has object-fit:contain.
items.gain: Inference: fullscreen through --fullscreen is the surviving command (catalog:101).

items.name: iframe
items.what: The UA provides src and srcdoc, sandbox tokens, allow, loading, and a default 2px inset border.
items.gain: Sandboxed srcdoc for untrusted content.

items.name: canvas
items.what: A bitmap surface with transparent fallback content and a restricted interactive allowlist. A width reset clears it.
items.gain: none stated

lessons: The elements guide's own form notes pair each native form behavior with a factory step: requestSubmit validates and fires submit, `new FormData` fires formdata synchronously on every call, willValidate excludes disabled, unnamed, readonly, and button controls, and ValidityState is live, so stable message strings must be stored (forms.md:1024-1060).
Prefer requestSubmit() over submit(): submit() bypasses validation and the submit event (forms.md:412-416).
dialog closing: never remove the open attribute by hand. Route every close affordance through requestClose() so the cancel and close handlers hold all the logic (interactives.md:546-550, 576-580).
The spec forbids details for tab or menu widgets and dialog for menus, tooltips, or listboxes (interactives.md:64, 454).
Store machine values in data value= or time datetime= so a sorter reads keys, not display text (texts.md:1120-1130).
Table header association is computed by the UA algorithm from scope, headers, and row and column groups. A module must keep th scope and caption intact rather than replace them (tables.md:603-623).
Unknown: the content of the orkestrel form and table packages. Neither is installed in /home/user/veneer/node_modules, so every 'fit' is inference.

items.name: Popover API ([popover], :popover-open, popovertarget)
items.what: The [popover] panel surface: top layer, ::backdrop, light dismiss with popover=auto or manual. The entry and exit transition uses @starting-style plus transition-behavior: allow-discrete. Variants are the bare panel and [popover='hint']/[role='tooltip']. The @starting-style block sits one specificity step below :popover-open to get around a Chrome 148+ leak.
items.gain: One canonical chrome token set, --set-popover-*, used by menus, non-modal dialogs and drawers. Theme tracking. No JS is needed to open or dismiss.
items.overlap: popover.js, tooltip.js and dropdown.js (Bootstrap JS and component, so excluded under the overlap test). Inference.

items.name: CSS Anchor Positioning (implicit anchor via popovertarget, position-area, position-try-fallbacks, position-visibility)
items.what: Auto-anchored placement for [popover]:not(:where(aside,dialog,nav,output)). The default is position-area: block-end. Fallbacks flip-block, flip-inline, then both, with position-try-order normal. max-block-size 18rem and max-inline-size 28rem act as the demanded size. overflow:auto with overscroll-behavior:contain. position-visibility: anchors-visible. position:absolute rather than fixed.
items.gain: Placement with no Popper. .top/.bottom/.start/.end modifiers map to position-area. Placement layers carry position only and no paint.
items.overlap: Popper placement inside Bootstrap's dropdown, popover and tooltip (inference). A standalone positioning surface has no Bootstrap component.

items.name: ::backdrop (top layer scrim)
items.what: Dim scrim on dialog:modal::backdrop and :is(aside,nav)[popover]:popover-open::backdrop. The transition is declared on the bare pseudo so it survives the close tail. Tokens live on :root because ::backdrop does not inherit.
items.gain: A single-backdrop guarantee: no duplicate backdrop elements anywhere.
items.overlap: The source states Bootstrap parity with .modal-backdrop and .offcanvas-backdrop.

items.name: Scrollbar styling (scrollbar-color, scrollbar-width, scrollbar-gutter)
items.what: Defaults on :root, built from separate thumb and track tokens. ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudos are deliberately not used. Safari < 18.2 falls back to the native overlay scrollbar.
items.gain: Themed scrollbars and a stable gutter from tokens.

items.name: :focus-visible ring
items.what: A shared box-shadow ring tinted by the variant. It excludes input, textarea, select and table[role=grid] at zero specificity through :where(). Plain :focus is never styled. Under forced-colors an outline in Highlight is used.
items.gain: The same focus signal on every interactive element, and it survives forced colors.
items.overlap: Bootstrap focus-ring helper and $focus-ring vars in the sheet (inference). This is styling, not JS.

items.name: ::placeholder
items.what: Placeholder color is currentColor at opacity 0.6. Forced colors use GrayText. This replaced the per-element placeholder tokens.
items.gain: The placeholder follows the control's variant color.
items.overlap: Bootstrap form-control placeholder color (sheet only; inference).

items.name: ::marker
items.what: Marker color and content tokens. Notes the property whitelist. summary is kept out of reach: it uses a ::before mask SVG and hides ::-webkit-details-marker.
items.gain: Muted bullets and custom glyphs.

items.name: ::selection
items.what: A selection background tinted by the variant at 25% through color-mix. Tokens live on :root and are retuned by the variant context.
items.gain: Selection that matches the theme and the variant scope.

items.name: View Transitions (::view-transition-old/new, @view-transition navigation:auto)
items.what: A default cross-page fade. Duration and timing are tokens. Per-name overrides are written at the call site. Paired with reduced motion.
items.gain: Page transitions with no JS.

items.name: <dialog> (showModal/show, :modal, ::backdrop)
items.what: Composable useDialog: native showModal()/close() plus cancellable show and hide events. Layout is gated on :modal/[open]. Non-modal show() is the in-flow family.
items.gain: A modal with a focus trap and backdrop from the browser, cancellable lifecycle events, and modal and non-modal variants.

items.name: <aside popover> / <nav popover> (offcanvas drawer)
items.what: useAside: a popover top-layer drawer with four placements and a native ::backdrop. It works with the native popover alone. useAside adds a focus trap, scroll lock and configurable backdrop dismiss. The earlier [data-aside-open]/[data-aside-closing] machinery was removed and replaced by pure :popover-open gating.
items.gain: A drawer with no JS. Optional richer behavior.

items.name: <details>/<summary>
items.what: useDetails: [open] toggle and a height transition through interpolate-size. summary paints its own marker.
items.gain: An animated accordion over the native disclosure.

items.name: <menu popover> (dropdown/listbox)
items.what: useMenu/usePopover: a <menu popover> panel with arrow-key roving and anchor positioning. useSelect is a <menu> listbox with filtering, multi-select and autocomplete.
items.gain: Keyboard roving, plus a combobox over popover and anchor.
items.overlap: dropdown.js (inference). The combobox has no Bootstrap counterpart (inference).

items.name: <output popover> (toast)
items.what: useToast: <output popover=manual> with auto-hide and deck stacking. Implicit polite live region. Fixed to a viewport corner, so it is excluded from anchor positioning.
items.gain: A toast from native top layer and live-region semantics.

items.name: [popover='hint'] tooltip
items.what: useTooltip: hover and focus triggers with a [popover=hint] panel, inverted chrome.
items.gain: A tooltip on native popover=hint.

items.name: <select> (appearance: base-select, ::picker(select))
items.what: useSelect. The cascade covers both appearance:auto and Chromium 134+ base-select with ::picker(select) customization. Combobox filtering and click-to-select.
items.gain: A fully styleable native select picker.
items.overlap: form-select is styling only (sheet). No Bootstrap JS for select (inference).
items.fit: Inference: Orkestrel form package (select/combobox field). Not stated in the source.

items.name: <form> (Constraint Validation API)
items.what: useForm: orchestrates constraint validation. It mirrors [data-form-validated], sets aria-invalid on controls, gives a validity.errors summary and accepts custom rules through validity.mark(). Chrome includes label:has(:invalid).
items.gain: Native validation exposed as aria and data state, with an error summary and custom rules.
items.overlap: Bootstrap .was-validated and :invalid styling (sheet only, no JS; inference).
items.fit: Inference: Orkestrel form package. Not stated in the source.

items.name: <table> (role=grid)
items.what: useTable: sort, paginate, select, expand and resize. Sticky header, zebra rows, sortable headers and a density modifier. Under role=grid the table is the focus anchor while the cells are the visible target.
items.gain: Data-grid behavior over the native table.
items.overlap: Bootstrap .table is styling only. No Bootstrap JS for a data table (inference).
items.fit: Inference: Orkestrel table package. Not stated in the source.

items.name: <nav> + IntersectionObserver (scroll-spy)
items.what: useNav: IntersectionObserver plus aria-current='location' for active-link tracking.
items.gain: Scroll-spy on a native observer.

items.name: [role=tablist] tabs
items.what: useTabs: keyboard roving over [role='tablist'] and lazy mounting of panels.
items.gain: ARIA tabs.

items.name: HTML Drag and Drop
items.what: useDrag + useDrop: HTML5 drag and drop with reorder events.
items.gain: Reorder events over native drag and drop.

items.name: Pointer Events
items.what: usePointer: multiplexes pointerdown, then pointermove*, then pointerup.
items.gain: A single pointer gesture primitive.

items.name: Focus trap primitive
items.what: useFocus: an activate()/deactivate() tab-trap primitive.

lessons: Open-state gating: drawer-shaped CSS (display, position:fixed, large transforms) must be gated on :popover-open, :modal, [open] or [data-{name}-open]. Otherwise it defeats the UA's display:none and the element stays visible after close(). (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/elements.md:156; /home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:32,71)
Never put layout utilities (grid, flex, block) on a [popover] element itself. Put them on a child. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:101-111,337)

Keep @starting-style one specificity tier below :popover-open. A Chrome 148+ regression leaks starting-style into the cascade and can leave the popover at opacity 0. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:92)
Exclusion lists use zero-specificity :not(:where(...)). A raw :not(output) raises specificity and breaks the hint variant. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:338)
Put the backdrop transition on the bare ::backdrop, not on the open-state rule. Otherwise the backdrop flashes on close. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:188)

Single-backdrop invariant: use native ::backdrop only and never a duplicate scrim element. Tokens for pseudos generated outside the DOM go on :root. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:186,190,326)
Chrome and placement are separate sources: placement layers declare no paint properties. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:125)
Known limitation of anchor positioning: the flip does not re-evaluate when a nested container scrolls. Composables can nudge max-block-size. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:153)

Three layers, one job each: the composable owns state, composables/ owns state-gated chrome, and the element or component owns the static baseline. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:217)

What failed and was removed: the [data-aside-open]/[data-aside-closing] dual-attribute drawer machinery, replaced by pure :popover-open gating. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:43)

Contradiction: the useAside one-liner still says 'dual-attribute gating' (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:222) and elements.md:193 says 'dual-attribute lifecycle', while components.md:43 says that machinery was removed.

Toast and alert split: <output popover> overlays (top layer, polite). <aside role=alert> shifts the UI (in flow). Choose by family, not by tag. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:150-164)

The element is the component. Use class roots only when no semantic tag fits, and write down why. Slot classes are {root}-{slot}, and only for class roots. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:5-17,170-174,252)

Element-rule test: does preflight or the UA already do it? If so, no rule. If it is only an opinion, no rule. Add a rule only for a real semantic gap. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/elements.md:146-152)
Component-specific state uses native attributes where they exist ([open], [aria-busy]). The modifier vocabulary covers shared states. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/components.md:174)

Events (from the AGENTS.md context that loaded with the read, not from the three guides): CustomEvent on the host element named elements:{source}:{verb}, with a single-word verb from a closed vocabulary. emit() is not cancelable and dispatch() is cancelable for pre-transition gates. Options.on holds initial listeners. 4 to 8 events per entity. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/AGENTS.md §14)

Naming (AGENTS.md): every property, method, option key and event is a single word. Group options by an entity key. Lifecycle verbs have no synonyms. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/AGENTS.md §4.1, §8, §11)
Don't style plain :focus. Rely on :focus-visible, and pair it with a forced-colors outline. (/home/user/mikesaintsg/elements/guides/surfaces.md:248-250)
The 'ghost' style was dropped because it failed WCAG AA on 4 of 7 variants in dark mode (AGENTS.md §21.4, not the three guides).

results.source: /home/user/scaffold/guides/form.md (read whole, lines 1-1792). The guide does not state the version 0.0.8. The browser systems are named only where the guide names them (Constraint API, validity, FormData, the submitter, datalist, datetime-local, range). The guide never mentions showPicker, inputmode, autocomplete, output, :user-invalid, requestSubmit, or the formdata event; those items are labelled inference and have no browser-spec citation, because this read covered the guide alone.

items.name: @orkestrel/form core surface a browser host consumes
items.what: Environment-agnostic document made of FormSchema, Form, declarative FieldRule data, and one submit that settles once. createForm(schema, options) returns a FormInterface. Its data members are emitter, schema, values, baseline, errors, touched, disabled, status, valid, and dirty, plus answer. Its methods are field, fill, touch, invalidate, disable, enable, submit, clear, and destroy. Nothing in the package renders, reads a keyboard, or opens a socket.
items.gain: A veneer host module can bind Bootstrap form markup to one owned, validated, serializable document instead of writing its own validation state.
items.overlap: Bootstrap 5.3 validation styles (.was-validated, .is-invalid, .invalid-feedback). Bootstrap has no form-state JavaScript.

items.name: Browser binding (src/browser) as the owner of rendering
items.what: The concept inventory assigns these to src/browser: binding a schema to real elements (taking a form and an element), the Constraint-API binding, and FormData with duplicate names. The guide also assigns accessibility IDs, first-error focus, input masks, and presentation hints to the renderer. Rendering is the browser's contribution and does not live in the package.
items.gain: Defines exactly what a veneer host module would own: element ids and their label/help links, focus, the error display policy, and the reflection of constraints onto elements.

items.name: Constraint Validation API (validity, required/min/max/step/pattern attributes)
items.what: The guide calls reflecting required and minimum onto real elements and reading validity back 'binding work' that 'belongs where the elements are'. It warns that the package's required model differs from HTML on purpose: HTML fails required on the exact empty string, and the package counts '' as an answer.
items.gain: A host can mirror FieldRule onto native attributes for the native UI and accessibility. It must still treat form.errors as the authority and project blank values through matchesAnswer.
items.overlap: Bootstrap uses :invalid/:valid through .was-validated and adds no JavaScript beyond its example snippet

items.name: :user-invalid display timing
items.what: Inference: the guide never names :user-invalid. It says the touched set exists so a renderer can hold a message back until somebody has visited the field. A failed submit marks every enabled field touched. When to show errors is host policy over touched.
items.gain: Inference: :user-invalid gives native timing that matches the touched policy without JavaScript. The guide's model is form.touched.
items.overlap: Bootstrap .was-validated shows every state at once after submit

items.name: requestSubmit and the submit act
items.what: Inference for requestSubmit, which the guide does not name. The guide says submit is the commit and not the attempt. A network attempt belongs to the host, runs before submit, and reports refusal through invalidate. Request states (idle, submitting, succeeded, failed) belong to the host and are held beside the form.
items.gain: A host module intercepting the native submit event can follow the guide's sequence: a sync submit() check, then the host request, then invalidate on refusal, then submit() on success.

items.name: FormData and the formdata event
items.what: The guide assigns several values under one name, the submitter button, and the FormData encoding to src/browser. FormValues holds one answer per field name by design. parseValue coerces numeric strings and 'true'/'false' for wire input. parseValues is strict and returns undefined on an unknown key. The formdata event itself is not named (inference).
items.gain: A host can read FormData and pass it through parseValues or parseValue. Checkbox groups (multi-value names) become a readonly string[].

items.name: Native input types (date, time, datetime-local, color, range, checkbox, radio, file)
items.what: The control mapping is as follows. datetime is datetime-local with no zone. A lone checkbox and a switch are both confirm. checkbox is the multi-choice group. A radio group is select. A range is number with minimum, maximum, and step all set. color is #rrggbb. file holds names only. Temporal patterns are lexical, and the host's date control refuses an impossible day.
items.gain: The renderer picks the native affordance from the field. It never invents a control, and value parsing and localization are the binding's job.

items.name: datalist
items.what: A datalist is a select with open: true, which the guide reads as 'suggest these, accept anything'. A disabled choice is shown and refused at every door. Live or fetched choices mean the host builds a new schema, and parseForm audits it.
items.gain: A host can render open selects as an input with a datalist.
items.overlap: Bootstrap styles .form-control with datalist, no JS

items.name: showPicker, inputmode, autocomplete, output
items.what: Not named in the guide (inference). The guide puts presentation hints and input masks with the renderer. It says meta is the bounded JSON carrier for renderer hints, that evaluation never reads meta, and that the package defines no key in it. Tel and search are text with no rule.
items.gain: Inference: a host could carry inputmode or autocomplete hints in field meta under host-owned keys and call showPicker for date, time, and color controls.

lessons: The renderer owes each field its label, its help, one message per FieldError keyed by rule, and a display policy over touched that holds messages back until the field is visited (form.md:550-553).
hidden means omit but still validate and submit. locked means render without edits. disabled means the field is out of evaluation and submission. fill accepts all three (form.md:1005-1015).
Project blank input at the binding with fill(name, matchesAnswer(raw) ? raw : undefined). Core evaluation never applies HTML's empty-string model (form.md:647-676, 1673-1677).
submit is the commit, not the attempt. Run the request first, report a refusal with invalidate, and call submit only after success. Request states belong to the host (form.md:1312-1336).
Read errors from the returned submit result rather than from form.errors when validate listeners write. The two can disagree (form.md:1300-1304, 1319-1323).
First-error focus belongs to the renderer. errors is ordered by schema and then by rule, so the first entry is the first error (form.md:1734).
Accessibility ids belong to the layer that owns the elements (form.md:1733).
Trimming, normalization, and value localization belong to the binding (form.md:1748-1750).
A file value holds names only. Bytes belong to the host's transport (form.md:267, 1735).
Pick an affordance by category, not by control name. A renderer never invents a control. Range is shown only when minimum, maximum, and step are all set (form.md:543-585).
Put host renderer hints in meta under host-owned keys. The package never reads meta (form.md:474-506).
Branch on FormError.code through isFormError, never on message text, and never parse auditSchema strings (form.md:888-891, 1586-1588).
Parse untrusted schemas with parseForm, and bound the payload size at the transport. Pattern time is unbounded (form.md:762-766, 831-838).

Read-only. Overlap column is inferred against Bootstrap 5.3 (labelled 'inferred'); veneer fit is inferred unless noted.

items.name: Popover API ([popover], showPopover/hidePopover/togglePopover, beforetoggle/toggle)
items.what: usePopover/createPopover adds programmatic show/hide, anchor positioning, click-outside dismiss, and placement events. It is the base for menu, tooltip, and select. useAside is a thin shim over the Popover API: the native beforetoggle/toggle events are bridged, and light-dismiss, top layer, ::backdrop and the slide are left to the platform.
items.gain: Native top-layer, light-dismiss and toggle events with no JS geometry. The guide reports that removing redundant JS state cut close latency from about 400 ms to about 73 ms.
items.overlap: Bootstrap popover.js, offcanvas.js, dropdown.js (inferred; all excluded by the overlap test)

items.name: CSS anchor positioning (position-area, position-try-fallbacks)
items.what: An anchor-position surface with required tokens gap, max-block-size, max-inline-size, position-area, position-try-fallbacks, position-try-order and viewport-inset. Placement modifiers emit position-area, align-self and justify-self directly. Menus, popovers and tooltips are anchor-positioned.
items.gain: Floating placement without a Popper-style JS engine
items.overlap: Popper inside Bootstrap's tooltip, popover and dropdown (inferred)

items.name: <dialog> showModal/show/close, :modal, cancel event
items.what: useDialog runs the modal and non-modal lifecycle. It adds Escape dismiss (through the cancel event), backdrop-click dismiss including a 'static' option, scroll lock for non-modal dialogs, and a cancellable show/hide plus a prevent event.
items.gain: Builds on the native modal, focus handling and ::backdrop instead of reimplementing them

items.name: <details>/[open], toggle event, ::details-content, interpolate-size
items.what: useDetails keeps [open] in sync with the native toggle event and adds optional accordion grouping. The height animation is pure CSS through interpolate-size and ::details-content.
items.gain: An accordion or disclosure with no JS height tween

items.name: Constraint Validation API (<form>, validity, invalid, formdata, reset)
items.what: useForm drives the native validation pipeline. It adds: a [data-form-validated] marker after the first attempt (parity with Bootstrap's .was-validated); aria-invalid on every field; reactive data, dirty, touched, valid and validated refs; per-field validity.errors; validity.mark(name, message) for custom, cross-field and server rules; fields.focus, enable and disable; and both reset() (native form.reset) and clear(). It captures invalid events in the capture phase because invalid does not bubble, and it dispatches a cancellable submit carrying {data, errors, valid}.
items.gain: A reactive validation state and error summary over the native API
items.overlap: Bootstrap validation styles (.was-validated, CSS only; no JS family) (inferred)
items.fit: An orkestrel form package is the likely carrier (inferred; the package was not read)

items.name: <table> (aria-sort, aria-rowcount/rowindex, pointer capture, roving tabindex)
items.what: useTable adds: single and shift-multi-column sort with an aria-sort mirror, where data-sort-value overrides textContent; pagination with aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex; multi-select with shift, ctrl and cmd plus a data-no-select opt-out; inline cell editing; CSS-driven row expansion through interpolate-size and inert; column resize with pointer capture; and an APG roving-tabindex grid focus model.
items.gain: Interactive data-grid behaviour. Bootstrap only styles tables.
items.fit: An orkestrel table package is the likely carrier (inferred; the package was not read)

items.name: IntersectionObserver
items.what: useNav provides an IntersectionObserver scroll-spy that sets aria-current="location" on the active link. Options: intersection.offset, margin and threshold.
items.gain: Scroll-spy with semantic aria-current

items.name: HTML Drag and Drop (useDrag/useDrop)
items.what: An HTML5 drag-source pipeline over [data-index] rows that emits tap, start, over, drop, end and reorder. The drop zone tracks over with awareness of relatedTarget.
items.gain: Reorder events. relatedTarget-aware enter/leave avoids flicker on child elements.
items.overlap: none (inferred); veneer drags already covers this surface

items.name: Pointer Events (+ setPointerCapture)
items.what: usePointer multiplexes pointerdown, pointermove and pointerup and locks the body cursor during a drag. It is the stated basis for a splitter or slider, and it is reused for toast swipe-to-dismiss (with touch-action: pan-y) and table column resize.
items.gain: A gesture primitive for splitters, sliders and swipe

items.name: Focus management (tab-trap) and inert
items.what: useFocus is a tab-trap with activate() and deactivate(). The guide advises inert rather than aria-hidden for closed state: inert blurs descendants, removes them from the accessibility tree and blocks pointer events, while aria-hidden on a focused subtree causes Chrome warnings.
items.gain: Focus containment for surfaces that lack native focus management

items.name: prefers-color-scheme / theme root
items.what: useTheme is a singleton with two axes: a mode pin through data-mode (light, dark, or absent to follow the OS through CSS), and a palette through data-theme. It persists both, and its events are light, dark, system and name.
items.gain: The OS-follow default stays in CSS. JS only pins.
items.overlap: Bootstrap data-bs-theme color modes (CSS; the toggler is docs JS, not a component) (inferred)

items.name: prefers-reduced-motion
items.what: useReducedMotion is deliberately not shipped. The CSS transition mixin honours the media query, so a composable would be redundant. Every animated partial must use the transition or reduced-motion mixin.
items.gain: A rule to keep motion opt-out in CSS

items.name: aria-pressed toggle button
items.what: useButton handles toggle state and mirrors it to aria-pressed. It emits toggle.
items.gain: Minimal

items.name: [role=alert]/[role=status] live region
items.what: useAlert provides a dismiss lifecycle with [data-alert-dismiss] triggers and a cancellable show/hide. After close it sets aria-hidden so the live region stops announcing.
items.gain: Live-region hygiene

items.name: Toast on <div role=status popover>
items.what: useToast provides auto-hide, a deck stack, pause on hover or focus, and swipe-to-dismiss through createPointer. The host is a popover div, not <output>, because <output> is phrasing-only.
items.gain: A toast in the top layer through the Popover API

items.name: Tabs ([role=tablist])
items.what: Arrow-key roving focus, aria-selected toggling and lazy panel mount
items.gain: n/a

items.name: Carousel
items.what: Slide index, autoplay (ride, pause, interval), keyboard and touch input, a cancellable slide event, and aria-selected on the indicators
items.gain: n/a

items.name: Menu / Select (<menu popover>, combobox/listbox)
items.what: useMenu handles the dropdown, roving focus, Home/End keys and anchor placement. useSelect adds listbox and combobox modes, multi-select and autocomplete; filtering by data-hidden; an empty-state hint through :has(); an IME composition guard (compositionstart/compositionend); and a native <select>/<input> mirror that dispatches change so the value takes part in form data.
items.gain: An autocomplete combobox that still takes part in form data (Bootstrap has none). The menu part overlaps Bootstrap's dropdown.
items.overlap: Bootstrap dropdown.js for the menu (inferred); the combobox/autocomplete has no counterpart (inferred)
items.fit: Through its native form mirror, the select would compose with an orkestrel form package (inferred)

items.name: Tooltip ([popover=hint])
items.what: Hover and focus triggers, role=tooltip wiring through aria-describedby, anchor positioning and delays
items.gain: n/a

items.name: Open/closed lifecycle (dual-attribute gating, @starting-style, allow-discrete)
items.what: Three players share the lifecycle: the UA's display:none, author CSS, and the factory. The four invariants: the bare element rule stays minimal; the open state is gated on [data-x-open]/[data-x-closing] or on :popover-open, :modal or [open]; the closing attribute persists until the next show; and @starting-style targets a selector one specificity step lower, to work around a Chrome 148+ cascade leak. Gotchas: hidePopover() fires no transitionend when nothing changes (use a 400 ms fallback, or transition opacity), and layout utilities on [popover] defeat the UA's display:none.
items.gain: Prevents a ghost flash of a closed surface

items.name: View Transitions (::view-transition-old/new(root))
items.what: A surface with duration and timing-function tokens, animated with reduced-motion discipline
items.gain: Page or state transitions styled through tokens

items.name: Browser pseudo-element surfaces (::backdrop, ::marker, ::placeholder, ::selection, scrollbar, :focus-visible)
items.what: Each surface has a token namespace: the backdrop (background-color, backdrop-filter, transition), the marker, the placeholder, selection, the scrollbar (thumb, track, width, gutter) and the focus ring color
items.gain: A themable surface over browser chrome
items.overlap: Bootstrap styles some of these via Sass/CSS variables (inferred)

items.name: Factory + adapter split, CustomEvent emitter
items.what: A framework-agnostic create* factory paired with a thin use* Vue adapter. Events are CustomEvents named elements:{source}:{verb} from a closed verb vocabulary: dispatch is cancellable, emit is informational. destroy() is idempotent with a clean dispose, and assertElement rejects the wrong tag.
items.gain: n/a (structural guidance)

items.name: Data-attribute and JS-to-CSS parity
items.what: Every data-* attribute takes the form data-{factory-stem}-{...}. Every attribute a factory writes must be read by CSS, or it must be allow-listed as JS-only. The documented regressions are createAside's dead attributes plus a wait of about 400 ms, and createTabs toggling aria-hidden while the CSS read [hidden].
items.gain: n/a

lessons: Let the platform own the lifecycle. createAside was stripped to a shim once :popover-open, @starting-style and allow-discrete drove the slide; its redundant JS attributes added about 400 ms of dead wait (composables.md:241, composables.md:389).
Every JS-written state attribute must be read by CSS, or be justified as JS-only; otherwise drop the write (composables.md:101, composables.md:392).
Use inert, not aria-hidden, for closed surfaces (composables.md:252).
Do not ship a composable for something CSS already does, as with useReducedMotion (composables.md:45).
invalid does not bubble, so form validation must listen in the capture phase (composables.md:412).
A composable over <select> or a combobox should mirror into a native control and dispatch change so the value takes part in form data, and it should guard IME composition (composables.md:408).
Host choice must respect the content model: the toast uses a popover div because <output> is phrasing-only (composables.md:30).
Make events cancellable before the transition (show/hide) and informational after it (open/close), and keep verbs in a closed vocabulary (composables.md:52-62, composables.md:381).
Destroy must be idempotent and must reverse every listener, observer and timer (composables.md:103, composables.md:382).
Gate display and geometry on the open-state selector, and aim @starting-style at a selector one specificity step lower (composables.md:230-235).
Name options after their entity, one word each; split rather than compound (README.md:425; AGENTS.md §4.1-4.2, read via the hook context).

results.source: /home/user/scaffold/guides/table.md (read whole, lines 1-1557). The guide does not state the version string 0.0.7, and it never names aria-sort, a search landmark, Bootstrap, or veneer. Every binding to those is labelled INFERENCE.

items.name: @orkestrel/table core barrel (createTable, Table, TableInterface)
items.what: A tabular document that works in any environment. A TableSchema declares the columns, a Table holds the rows, and one lens of sort, filter, and page decides which rows the view shows. Nothing in it renders, measures, reads a keyboard, or names a host type. Everything the guide lists is exported from @orkestrel/table src/core. The manager classes are internal; the browser binding is planned for a future src/browser that takes a table and an element.
items.gain: A host module gets the whole data side of sorting, filtering, and paging. The host keeps only drawing. INFERENCE: a veneer module would take a TableInterface plus a Bootstrap .table element.
items.overlap: Bootstrap .table styles only. There is no Bootstrap table JavaScript. INFERENCE: a veneer table host has no JS counterpart, but the overlap test still needs a ruling on it.

items.name: TableSchema / TableColumn cells (text, number, flag, choice), hidden, meta, label, help
items.what: A column's cell type fixes how it compares and which filters apply. There is no sortable or filterable flag. The hidden flag tells the host whether to draw a column. meta is host-owned JSON the table never reads (for example alignment or a number format). label and help are the strings an accessible grid needs. Dates are ISO text.
items.gain: A host builds the thead from schema.columns and skips columns marked hidden. INFERENCE: meta can carry Bootstrap classes such as text-end. label goes in the th text.

items.name: Column sort binding (sort.order/orders/set/remove)
items.what: There is no verb that cycles a sort. The host reads the column's term, decides the next direction, and calls set or remove. Setting a direction on an already-sorted column replaces it in place. The sort is stable and allows several terms. Any change emits a sort event carrying the whole list of terms.
items.gain: A header-button host decides the next direction itself. INFERENCE: it writes aria-sort (ascending/descending/none) on the th from sort.order(column) and redraws on the sort event. The guide puts ARIA in the host's hands.

items.name: Filter input binding (filter.set/remove, admitsFilter, CellMatcher)
items.what: Filters combine with and only, one per column. contains is case-sensitive, so a host that wants to ignore case supplies a CellMatcher through TableOptions.matchers. admitsFilter lets a host ask in advance which operators a column takes and whether a typed value fits, before offering the control. filter.set raises CELL or COLUMN errors. A global search box that matches across all columns is out of scope: the host narrows rows() with its own predicate.
items.gain: A filter input calls filter.set or filter.remove, guarded by admitsFilter. INFERENCE: wrapping the filter controls in a search element or role=search is a host choice. The guide does not mention it.
items.fit: @orkestrel/table; INFERENCE @orkestrel/form for the filter controls (not read)

items.name: Pagination binding (pagination.page/limit/offset/count, move, resize)
items.what: Pages count from 1. pagination.count is max(1, ceil(rows/limit)), so the host can always show 'page 1 of 1'. A move past the end clamps to the last page. resize keeps the first visible row in view, and calling it with no argument stops paging. A paginate event fires whenever the page moves, including a clamp. table.count is the number of rows; pagination.count is the number of pages.
items.gain: INFERENCE: a Bootstrap .pagination nav draws pagination.count page links, marks the current one with active and aria-current=page, disables prev/next at the ends, and calls move(n). It redraws on the paginate event.

items.name: Events and lifecycle (emitter, on, error, clear, destroy, destroyed)
items.what: The events are write, remove, sort, filter, select, expand, paginate, and clear. Each fires after the change is committed, and a change that does nothing emits nothing. When one call emits several events, the order is rows first, then select, expand, paginate. clear emits only the clear event. destroy can be called more than once; after it, getters still answer. A listener that throws is isolated and reported to the error option.
items.gain: A host redraws from view in response to events instead of polling, and can check destroyed instead of catching errors.

items.name: Selection and expansion key sets
items.what: Both are TableKey sets that persist across sort, filter, and page changes, and drop keys when rows are removed. select() with no argument picks every row in the table, not just the visible ones. A header checkbox that should pick only the page passes the view's keys. Expansion records only which rows are open; drawing their detail is the host's job.

items.what: The host owns rendering, ARIA and roles, keyboard and focus, virtualization, column widths, sticky headers, number/date formatting, CSV export, async data, and the browser binding. Seams the package already exposes: column reorder and hiding through the schema and hidden, row drag through rows.move(key, index), server paging through the lens values, and case folding through a matcher or comparator. lessons: The host owns drawing, ARIA, roles, ids, keyboard, and focus. The table supplies only the label and help strings (table.md:10-11, 1482-1484).
There is no sort-cycle verb. A heading host reads sort.order(column), decides the next direction, then calls set or remove (table.md:632-635).
Before offering a filter control or accepting a typed value, ask admitsFilter. filter.set raises CELL for any filter admitsFilter refuses (table.md:725-729).
contains is case-sensitive. Supply a CellMatcher in TableOptions.matchers to ignore case, and a CellComparator to collate by locale (table.md:288-291, 449-490).
Read view after any change. It is computed in the order filter, then sort, then page, and is never stored (table.md:590-593, 1398-1402).
table.count counts rows that pass the filter. pagination.count counts pages and is always at least 1, so 'page 1 of 1' over an empty list needs no special case (table.md:133-135, 778-780).
A header checkbox meant to pick the page must pass the view's keys. select() with no argument picks every row in the table (table.md:819-821).
Redraw from events, which fire after commit and stay silent on a no-op. Seeded rows emit nothing (table.md:938-962).
Branch on TableError.code through isTableError. Never match on message text or on auditTable strings (table.md:1312-1313, 1208-1213).
A global search box across columns is out of scope. The host filters rows() with its own predicate (table.md:1490).
Persisting a lens (sort, filters, keys, page) belongs to the host, in its own format. The package ships no parser for it (table.md:1075-1081).
Row drag-and-drop ends in rows.move(key, index) (table.md:1488).
The planned browser binding takes a table and an element and lives in a future src/browser (table.md:1506).
